items.title: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics
items.text: Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024 Watched 28th September 2026
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Video
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: UMG / CommonUI
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: UI Material Lab
items.text:
• Epic sample project with UI material functions and examples.
  • Documentation
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Play Animation Forward / Reverse
items.text:
• Use for hover/unhover animations.
  • Plays from the current animation state instead of restarting.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Stack Box
items.text:
• Stacks children vertically or horizontally.
  • Can replace separate Vertical Box / Horizontal Box layouts in suitable cases.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Common Visual Attachment
items.text:
• Attaches a visual element without changing the layout size of the attached widget.
  • Useful for badges, markers, prompts, and similar overlays.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Common Text Block
items.text:
• Supports text overflow handling and marquee-style scrolling.
  • Use with hover/unhover events for interactive text.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Text Overflow Policy - Ellipsis
items.text: • Displays an ellipsis when text does not fit.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Wrap Box
items.text:
• Automatically wraps child widgets onto additional lines.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Spacer
items.text:
• Invisible layout widget used to take up space.
  • Useful for animating the position of other content.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Apply Line Height to Bottom Line
items.text:
• Controls whether line-height space is applied below the final line.
  • Useful for vertically centering multiline text.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Monospacing
items.text:
• Forces characters to use a consistent width.
  • Useful for text and animated numbers where changing character widths would cause movement.
  • Relevant font settings: bForceMonospaced, MonospacedWidth.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Common Numeric Text Block
items.text:
• Animates/interpolates numeric values.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Performance
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Global Invalidation
items.text:
• Reduces unnecessary UMG layout and paint work.
  • UE 5.8 guidance
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Slate Prepass
items.text:
• Some widgets and layouts require additional measurement passes.
  • Watch for Scale Box, Size Box, Rich Text, and auto-wrapped text.
  • Talk example: approximately 577 µs → 24 µs after removing an expensive layout setup.
  • UE 5.8 guidance
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Snap to Pixel
items.text: • Disable for smoother animated or scrolling text when sub-pixel movement is desirable.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Editor Utility Widgets
items.text:
• Create custom editor tools and dockable editor panels using UMG.
  • Documentation
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Slate Postbuffers
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Slate Postbuffers
items.text:
• Used for UI blur and other post-process effects.
  • Effects can be layered.
  • UE 5.8: Experimental.
  • Supports up to 5 Slate postbuffers.
  • Documentation
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Post Buffer Update
items.text:
• Controls where and when a Slate postbuffer is populated.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Slate Post Processors
items.text:
• Process Slate postbuffers.
  • Includes USlatePostBufferBlur.
  • UE 5.8 API
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Sampling Slate Postbuffers
items.text: • UI materials can sample GetSlatePost0 through GetSlatePost4.
path: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics

items.title: Examples
items.text:
• Epic's Content Examples project includes UI_SlatePostBuffer.
  • Examples include blur, masking, tinting, vignettes, and distortion.
  • Effects can be layered.

items.title: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'
items.text: Unreal Fest Orlando 2025 Watched 28th September 2026
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Video
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Important Notes
items.text:
1. This is for a game released in 2022 that was likely in development from 2019 onwards
  2. It uses a very game engine style component system
  3. Game Engines have started to move towards a .NET MVVM UI Architecture the last few years, this preceeds that
  4. Too abstract to make sense for a year long project
  5. It doesn't use current UE5 Common UI
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Scale
items.text: Problem Type Screen Complexity Depth Amount of Screens Breadth
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Terminology
items.text: Term What is it? Screen Base of the UI system Widget Visual UI Element Control Interactable Widget Screen Component A class that provides functionality that can be added to a screen
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: User Interface Component System
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: The Problem - What do I need to do?
items.text:
Break UI Implementation into Components?

  • Get Data
  • Display Data
  • Respond to User Actions
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Getting Data - Data Screen Component
items.text:
• Retrieve Data
  • Comes back as a TArray*
  • Optional Filters and Transforms
    • I need to sort the data in a certain way
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Displaying Data - View Component
items.text:
• Create & Cache Widgets
  • Add to a Container
  • Give Data to Widgets
  • Provide Widget Callbacks
  • You create instances of widgets instead of just referencing a sub class
    • This gives you the variables every widget has
    • More flexible than choosing a class
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Responding - Action Screen Components
items.text:
• Gather Data required for action
  • Determine if action can happen
  • Executing the action
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Communication
items.text:
• Get Components through Functions
  • Delegates
  • Component Selectors
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Get Components through Functions
items.text:
All Screens, Widgets and Screen Components have

  • ScreenComponentType* GetScreenComponent()
  • TArray GetAllScreenComponents()
  • ScreenComponentType* GetScreenComponentByName(FName)

    These are all available in Blueprints aswell
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Delegates
items.text:
So components can communicate between each other

  • OnDataRetrieved
  • OnClick
  • OnFocus
  • OnActionAttempt
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Component Selectors
items.text: Gives you a list of all the components on the screen you're editing so you can select what you want to listen to
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Character Select Example
items.text:
What do we want to do?

  1. Get a list of all characters unlocked
  2. Display them
  3. When selected display them on a screen

What happens?

  1. Data Screen Component fetches the unlocked heroes
  2. It fires of it's delegate when completed
  3. The view screen component is listening to this
  4. It will create the buttons and send the data so the icons can appear
  5. When someone clicks on one of the icons, the view screen broadcasts the action saying this is whats clicked heres the data
  6. The action screen component takes this and opens the character selected screen in response

The System is Data Driven as its designed to avoid boilerplate. No C++ or Blueprints needed.

The Character Inventory screen then has all of these, but it also has an entry screen component. This allows it to broadcast out that it's data has been changed so it is entry as data can be entered.

Why is this good?

  1. It simplifies the interactions between screens
  2. You don't need to know anything about the screens themselves
  3. You only need to know about the component you want to interact with
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.text:
• Composable Widget
    • Widget Layer
    • Widget Layer
    • Widget Layer

Allows layers to be independant and put in different configurations.

path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: Not all screens
items.text: Settings screens are well trotten ground you don't need to over complicate it, just make them like usual.
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'

items.title: How did UICS work for them
items.text:
• There is a bit of initial set up due to it being Data Driven
  • Once it was set up it was more efficient and took less effort
    • Easier to share functionality across screens
    • Data permutations
  • Learning Curve
    • About 3 Months
  • Consistency and workflow for UI Creation
  • Less Defects
path: How to Build UI at Scale: Lessons from Marvel’s 'Midnight Suns'
